name: Mirtazapine
summary: An atypical antidepressant (NaSSA) with prominent sedation and appetite stimulation — useful when sleep and appetite are impaired.
mechanism: Antagonizes presynaptic α2-adrenoceptors (increasing norepinephrine and serotonin release) plus 5-HT2, 5-HT3, H1, and α1 antagonism.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Sedation within hours; antidepressant effect 2–6 weeks

dosing.adult: 15 mg at bedtime to start; usual 15–45 mg/day at bedtime

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; no established major-malformation signal.
safety.lactation: Limited data; present in breast milk.
warnings: Black-box warning: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults (≤24 y) early in treatment
Somnolence — driving and falls risk, especially early on
Weight gain and increased appetite; lipid changes
Rare agranulocytosis/neutropenia — check CBC if fever or sore throat
monitoring: Mood and suicidality early in treatment
safety.overdose: Generally well tolerated in overdose; sedation and tachycardia are the main effects.

clinicalPearls: Lower doses (7.5–15 mg) are more sedating (H1); higher doses add noradrenergic activation.
Low sexual dysfunction — a useful alternative when SSRI sexual side effects are the problem.
good: Depression with insomnia, poor appetite, or weight loss; SSRI-intolerant patients.
bad: Patients who need daytime alertness or who are already overweight or metabolically at risk.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard psychopharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
